newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse eases as sellers stay dominant.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse eases as sellers stay dominant.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20 share index eased 0.55 points to 3,039.25 on Thursday as sellers continued to dominate the market, brokers said.
On average prices on key shares eased marginally, reflecting the mood.
"When prices are so low in the market as they are now, people normally want to sell, to guard against any further loss," a senior broker said.
"December is coming soon and most people need money, so they will sell," said another broker.
Bourse officials and brokers said activity in the market picked up slightly with a slight increase in deals.
Turnover was posted at 10.804 million shillings traded on 267,177 shares from 9.030 million shillings traded on 243,385 shares on Wednesday.
"We are worried. Lately any high turnover is because of special lots being traded in the market otherwise the normal turnover cannot even reach 20 million shillings on average," one broker said.
Oil concern Total Kenya traded 2,150 shares at 66.50 from 68.50 while Kenya National Mills traded 844 shares at 46.25 from 47.75.

Foreigners continue to dominate the Kenya Breweries and Kenya Commercial Bank. Some 29,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank were traded at between 55.50 and 56 while 1,100 shares of Kenya Breweries were traded at 50.
In commercials, Uchumi traded 92,500 shares at 45.75 from 45.50 while 33,140 shares of Kenya Airways were traded at 9.50 from 9.65.
